reason: All 17 bills, including every heavy one (rows 1-4), create or widen a civil route to forming or dissolving a couple outside the religious courts. Rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 14 are civil marriage or marriage-and-divorce laws. Rows 3 and 8-10 set up or widen a civil union, including one for people who cannot marry under religious law. Rows 11-13 and 17 allow civil weddings on embassy premises, row 12 allows registering civil marriages in Eilat, and row 15 calls a referendum on equality in marriage and divorce. The statement asks whether couples may marry in Israel without a religious ceremony, which is what these bills do, and it names the price (no recognition by the Chief Rabbinate). The bills also cover civil unions and divorce, but those are means to the same end, a civil option for personal status, and the statement covers them well enough. The direction of every label matches the agree key.
